scope.description: Source-level program inventory of eight pinned Chialisp primer/concept tutorials. Three closed Intro expressions have executed Cargo/native/original-reference/CLVM evidence; the other nine programs, one naming variant and supporting host workflows remain unimplemented or unrun. The nine original teaching fixtures are a separate corpus.
scope.coverage: Eight tutorial pages only; reference pages, primitives, CHIP implementations, linked include libraries and host workflows are not claimed complete.
scope.promotion_requirement: Each promotion requires exact pinned source extraction, current Cargo Rust/reference/manifest/report hashes, explicit ABI and semantic scope, independent original/native/CLVM comparisons and appropriate ledger evidence. Individual expression evidence does not complete a tutorial page or CHIP.
scope.recommended_contract: The three initial closed-expression ports use an explicit ignored-environment nullary ABI, accepting arbitrary CLVM trees without decoding them as Rust parameters. Evidence covers eight explicit adversarial environments and 256 generated bounded trees per expression; this finite testing is not a compiler-preservation proof.

examples.title: Construct the fixed list (1 2 3)
examples.feasibility: Implemented as a real Cargo nullary Rust export with an explicit ignored-environment ABI.
semantic_gaps: The original expression and this export both ignore arbitrary CLVM environments. The explicit ignored ABI is distinct from the default strict Rust tuple ABI and exposes no raw environment to Rust.
Rust u64 arithmetic is bounded; these fixed closed constants fit exactly. This port does not add general unbounded integers, raw-tree parameters or dynamic list support.
The report records finite differential observations, not a compiler-preservation or universal equivalence proof. This data-producing expression has no ledger authorization or conservation claim.
notes: The unwrapped original expression is extracted exactly from the pinned shell command and compiled using the upstream expression compilation stage; the shell run command itself is not executed.
Eight explicit environments and 256 deterministic bounded trees are compared through native Cargo Rust, optimized/unoptimized Rust and Rue CLVM, and independently compiled original Chialisp.

examples.title: Add two module arguments
examples.feasibility: Small bounded experiment after specifying the integer and environment observation contract.
semantic_gaps: Original arithmetic interprets atoms as signed, unbounded CLVM integers, including byte encodings outside a bounded canonical Rust integer ABI. Width, overflow, negative and padded-atom domains require an explicit comparison contract.
The original module argument pattern is not an exact canonical Rust decoder; extra environment fields, malformed shapes and raw atom/tree behavior must be observed separately.

examples.title: Recursive factorial
examples.feasibility: Requires recursion support, integer semantics and explicit execution-cost bounds.
semantic_gaps: Original arithmetic interprets atoms as signed, unbounded CLVM integers, including byte encodings outside a bounded canonical Rust integer ABI. Width, overflow, negative and padded-atom domains require an explicit comparison contract.
The original module argument pattern is not an exact canonical Rust decoder; extra environment fields, malformed shapes and raw atom/tree behavior must be observed separately.
Runtime recursion is unsupported by the current compiler; negative inputs and growth/cost must not be silently narrowed.
notes: The source code returns 1 when number <= 1; the surrounding prose/comments describe different base-case thresholds. Preserve the pinned code and investigate that discrepancy rather than silently repairing the lesson.

examples.title: Password-gated arbitrary conditions
examples.feasibility: Requires SHA256, currying and arbitrary tree/condition semantics; intentionally insecure teaching policy.
semantic_gaps: The original module argument pattern is not an exact canonical Rust decoder; extra environment fields, malformed shapes and raw atom/tree behavior must be observed separately.
SHA256 accepts the original password bytes rather than a fixed 32-byte message type.
The returned conditions are attacker-supplied CLVM values, not a fixed heterogeneous tuple.
Currying and its serialized/tree-hash contract are not implemented by the current compiler.
notes: Preserve the warning that plaintext passwords are exposed and a farmer can redirect unsigned conditions; never mark this as a secure payment pattern.

The original module argument pattern is not an exact canonical Rust decoder; extra environment fields, malformed shapes and raw atom/tree behavior must be observed separately.
Currying changes the program tree and hash; source equivalence does not imply committed module/instance hash identity.

examples.title: Signature wrapper around a runtime inner puzzle
examples.feasibility: Requires runtime apply, dynamic trees, tree hashing, currying and separately pinned include libraries.
semantic_gaps: Runtime CLVM apply and a dotted inner-solution tail are outside the current fixed tuple ABI.
sha256tree must hash arbitrary CLVM trees with pinned semantics; a fixed Message32 wrapper is insufficient.
BLS signature and ledger checks require the coin/network-bound message context, not just successful puzzle execution.
notes: The message commits to inner_solution, while the inner puzzle is separately curried into the wrapper.

examples.title: Return arbitrary supplied conditions
examples.feasibility: Requires arbitrary tree passthrough and an explicit original-vs-typed ABI observation contract.
semantic_gaps: The original module argument pattern is not an exact canonical Rust decoder; extra environment fields, malformed shapes and raw atom/tree behavior must be observed separately.
The result can be an arbitrary supplied CLVM tree; no finite condition tuple captures its full behavior.
notes: The upstream page explicitly labels this unsafe on its own because anyone can choose the conditions.

examples.title: Recursively double CREATE_COIN outputs
examples.feasibility: Requires runtime inner-puzzle apply, recursive condition traversal and dynamic list/tree semantics.
semantic_gaps: Original arithmetic interprets atoms as signed, unbounded CLVM integers, including byte encodings outside a bounded canonical Rust integer ABI. Width, overflow, negative and padded-atom domains require an explicit comparison contract.
Dynamic condition parsing, recursion and runtime apply are unsupported by the current compiler.
The source rewrites CREATE_COIN as exactly three fields, discarding optional fields such as memos; atom/improper-list tails need observations.
Doubling output requests does not itself establish aggregate funding, conservation or ledger validity.
notes: The surrounding filename says coin-doubler.clsp while the code-fence title says coin-double.clsp; retain this source discrepancy.

examples.title: Sign the tree hash of arbitrary conditions
examples.feasibility: Requires arbitrary conditions/tree hashing, currying, BLS ledger validation and separately pinned includes.
semantic_gaps: The original module argument pattern is not an exact canonical Rust decoder; extra environment fields, malformed shapes and raw atom/tree behavior must be observed separately.
The signature message is sha256tree of arbitrary conditions rather than an externally supplied fixed byte message.
The original returns a variable condition list; runtime list composition and arbitrary tree types are not implemented.
notes: This signs conditions before the outer coin-doubler transforms them; preserve that composition when studying authorization and output semantics.
